question: What fishery evidence does Mendoza et al. (2019) provide for the selected Pampanga riverine municipalities, and is it resolved enough for waterbody-specific species records?

source.citation: Mendoza, D. M., Mendoza, G. C., & Sarmiento, R. B. (2019). Traditional Fishing Gears in Selected Riverine Areas of Pampanga, Philippines. PSAU Journal of Research, 4(1), 37–50.
source.journalMetadataCrosscheck: PSAU Quality Assurance Office publication inventories identify the article in PSAU Journal of Research, volume 4, issue 1, 2019, pages 37–50. The article title and authors were checked in the journal viewer copy.

publisherIssueViewerPagesReviewed.contentReviewed: Title, author line, abstract and introductory scope.
Interview methods, locality frame, source of catch identifications, and gear context.
Catch-composition discussion and Table 5 through the public text-viewer extraction.

source.retrievalBoundary: The PSAU Quality Assurance Office viewer text was reviewed. No original PDF or page image was downloaded or retained, so the extracted Table 5 row count has not been visually verified.

studyScope.waterbodyTypeAsReported: Selected riverine areas. The introduction discusses the Pampanga River Basin and interconnected channels as broader provincial context, but the reviewed methods and catch table do not name capture channels, barangays, stations, or a taxon-to-channel crosswalk.
studyScope.fieldDates: No field or interview dates were found in the reviewed article pages.

respondents.selectionDescription: Fishers were selected based on fishing as their primary livelihood; a questionnaire supported the interviews.

methodsAndLimitations.catchIdentification: The article says fishers identified catch composition; photographs of samples were taken and compared with the FAO FishBase and SeaLifeBase electronic publications (2014). The reviewed pages provide no museum voucher or accession identifiers.
methodsAndLimitations.evidenceType: Historical, fisher-reported fishing-gear and catch-composition evidence at municipality level; not a standardized river reach, lake, wetland, or estuary fish survey.
methodsAndLimitations.taxonToWaterbodyResolution: Table 5 reports municipality-level presence marks. The reviewed pages provide no sampling station names, channel-level assignments, coordinates, or independently documented capture events.
methodsAndLimitations.countConflict: The abstract reports 33 finfish species and 14 crustacean species. The public text-viewer extraction exposes 32 fish-labelled entries and 14 crustacean-labelled entries in Table 5. Because the source page image was not inspected, the apparent one-fish difference may reflect a missed or merged viewer-text row; the count remains unresolved.
methodsAndLimitations.sourceReportedCaveat: The article says catch-diversity data rely mainly on fisher statements and that their claims still need validation. Its gear-specific peak-season biomass summary is not a standardized estimate of fish abundance, current presence, catchability, or fishing success.

rights.itemSpecificReuseLicense: No article-specific open reuse license was identified in the reviewed journal viewer pages or publication metadata.
rights.handling: Retain concise attributed findings and bibliographic links only. Do not redistribute the article, Table 5, journal photographs, or extracted catch dataset without permission. Public viewer access is not a reuse grant.

nextAction: Obtain an authorized, page-quality copy; visually reconcile the abstract and Table 5 counts; preserve all printed labels before cross-checking taxonomy; seek field dates, exact capture channels, voucher/photo provenance, and item-specific reuse terms. Keep all catch claims as historical fisher reports unless independent site-resolved evidence supports a stronger record.

sources.supports: PSAU Journal of Research viewer pages for the article title/authors and abstract, interview frame and catch-identification method, source-reported locality granularity and Table 5 count conflict. PSAU Quality Assurance Office publication inventory cross-checks the 2019 volume/issue/pages.
